exposure: interval time from transvaginal radiofrequency ablation to pregnancy
cohort: 226 pregnant patients who had previously undergone transvaginal radiofrequency ablation of leiomyomas between January 1, 2017, and February 28, 2022.
finding: Pregnancy outcomes after transvaginal radiofrequency ablation of leiomyomas were generally similar to those of a general population, with no instances of uterine rupture, placental abruption, or fetal growth restriction, though a shorter interval to pregnancy (<5.7 months) was associated with an increased miscarriage rate.
mod_finding: The cesarean delivery rate was 26.4%, with the remaining patients having normal spontaneous vaginal deliveries.
